rules.name: User temporary files
rules.hint: Deletes files older than 24 hours from your user temp folder. Files that are in use are skipped.
rules.description: Removes leftover files in %TEMP% that installers and apps forgot to delete. Only files older than 24 hours (by both creation and last-write time) are touched, files in use are skipped, and empty subfolders are removed. Deleted files cannot be restored; apps recreate what they need.
rules.sideEffects: An app that was paused mid-task for over a day may need to restart that task.

rules.name: Windows temporary files
rules.hint: Deletes files older than 24 hours from C:\Windows\Temp (needs admin). Files in use are skipped.
rules.description: Removes old files from the system temp folder used by Windows services and installers. Only files older than 24 hours are deleted and locked files are skipped. Deleted files cannot be restored; Windows recreates what it needs.

rules.name: Windows Error Reporting (your reports)
rules.hint: Removes queued and archived crash reports for your account. Keep them if you are troubleshooting a crash.
rules.description: Deletes your Windows Error Reporting archive and queue (crash and hang reports already sent or waiting). They are only useful while troubleshooting; Reliability Monitor keeps its summary. Deleted reports cannot be restored.
rules.sideEffects: Unsent crash reports for your account are discarded.

rules.name: Windows Error Reporting (system reports)
rules.hint: Removes system-wide crash and hang reports (needs admin). Keep them if you are troubleshooting a crash.
rules.description: Deletes the machine-wide Windows Error Reporting archive, queue and temp folders under ProgramData. These reports can be large after app or driver crashes. Deleted reports cannot be restored.
rules.sideEffects: Unsent system crash reports are discarded.

rules.name: Delivery Optimization cache
rules.hint: Empties the Delivery Optimization cache with Windows' own cmdlet (needs admin). Updates still download normally.
rules.description: Runs Delete-DeliveryOptimizationCache, the supported way to empty the cache that Windows Update and Store downloads use. Windows refills it only as needed. Nothing to revert: the cache is rebuilt automatically.
rules.sideEffects: Content in the cache is downloaded again if it is needed later.

rules.name: Windows Update download cache
rules.hint: Clears downloaded update files; stops and restarts Windows Update, BITS and DO (admin). Fixes stuck downloads.
rules.description: Deletes the contents of C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\Download, which is Microsoft's documented step for resetting stuck Windows Update downloads. The Windows Update, BITS and Delivery Optimization services are stopped first and always restarted afterwards. Pending updates download again.
rules.sideEffects: Updates that were already downloaded are downloaded again.

rules.name: Component store cleanup (DISM)
rules.hint: Runs DISM StartComponentCleanup to remove superseded update components (admin). Can take several minutes.
rules.description: Uses Repair-WindowsImage -StartComponentCleanup, the supported way to shrink the WinSxS component store. It removes superseded component versions that Windows would also clean on its own schedule. iG Windows Tuner never deletes inside WinSxS directly. Updates installed in the last 30 days stay uninstallable.
rules.sideEffects: Older superseded update versions can no longer be restored.

rules.name: Component store cleanup with /ResetBase
rules.hint: DISM cleanup with ResetBase: frees the most space but makes all installed updates permanent (no uninstall).
rules.description: Runs StartComponentCleanup with ResetBase, which removes every superseded component version. All currently installed updates become permanent and cannot be uninstalled. Use it only on a stable system you do not need to roll back.
rules.sideEffects: Installed updates can no longer be uninstalled.

rules.name: Previous Windows installation (Windows.old)
rules.hint: Shows the size of Windows.old and upgrade leftovers. Remove them in Settings to keep Windows' own rollback logic.
rules.description: Reports the size of C:\Windows.old and the upgrade staging folders. Removing them deletes your ability to go back to the previous Windows version, so iG Windows Tuner hands this to Windows itself: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > Previous Windows installation(s).
rules.sideEffects: Removing it (in Settings) makes the upgrade permanent.
rules.notes: Guidance only: use Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > Previous Windows installation(s).

rules.name: Crash dumps (minidumps and live kernel reports)
rules.hint: Deletes old crash dumps but keeps the newest one (admin). Keep all dumps while you investigate a BSoD.
rules.description: Deletes minidumps and live kernel reports created after blue screens and driver hangs, keeping the newest file for diagnosis. Full MEMORY.DMP is removed by Windows in Settings > Temporary files. Deleted dumps cannot be restored.
rules.sideEffects: Older crash dumps are no longer available for analysis.

rules.name: Servicing logs (CBS and DISM)
rules.hint: Removes old servicing log files and their compressed archives (admin). The three newest files are kept.
rules.description: Deletes old CBS and DISM log files and their .cab archives. The newest three files are kept so recent servicing problems can still be diagnosed, and logs in use are skipped. Deleted logs cannot be restored.

rules.name: Thumbnail cache
rules.hint: Deletes Explorer thumbnail caches so they are rebuilt. Files Explorer has open are skipped; icons are untouched.
rules.description: Deletes the thumbcache_*.db files that Explorer uses for picture and video previews. Use it when thumbnails look wrong or the cache has grown large. Explorer rebuilds thumbnails as you browse, so folders with many pictures load slower once. The icon cache is never touched.
rules.sideEffects: Thumbnails are regenerated the next time you open those folders.

rules.name: Icon cache
rules.hint: Deletes Explorer's icon cache files so blank or wrong icons are rebuilt. Files in use are skipped; use the Toolkit fix to restart Explorer.
rules.description: Deletes the iconcache_*.db files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer, the step Microsoft documents for blank desktop, Start and taskbar icons. Explorer keeps the files open while it runs, so the Toolkit fix 'Rebuild icon and thumbnail caches' closes Explorer first and starts it again afterwards. Windows rebuilds the cache as icons are shown.
rules.sideEffects: Icons are redrawn from the original files once; the desktop may flicker while Explorer restarts.

rules.name: Recycle Bin (all drives)
rules.hint: Empties your Recycle Bin on every fixed drive. Restore anything you still need first; this cannot be undone.
rules.description: Empties the current user's Recycle Bin on each fixed drive with Clear-RecycleBin. Files in the Recycle Bin are permanently deleted. Storage Sense can do this automatically for items older than 30 days instead.
rules.sideEffects: Deleted files can no longer be restored from the Recycle Bin.

rules.name: Old driver packages
rules.hint: Removes older third-party driver versions not used by any device, via pnputil without /force (admin).
rules.description: Finds third-party driver packages that have a newer version of the same package installed and are not bound to any present device. It removes them with pnputil /delete-driver without /force, so Windows refuses anything in use. Rolling a device back to a removed version then needs the old installer.
rules.sideEffects: Device Manager 'Roll Back Driver' can no longer return to the removed versions.
